theory.title: Exercise 2.2.4: Keywords with Return Values
theory.content:
📤 Getting Data Back

MENTOR-9: "PROTO-7, sometimes you don't just want keywords to DO things - you want them to TELL you things. That's what RETURN is for."

"A keyword can calculate a value, fetch data, or make a decision, then RETURN that information to whoever called it."

↩️ What is RETURN?

RETURN - Statement that sends a value back from a keyword to its caller

  • ✅ Data flow - Keywords can produce values
  • ✅ Calculations - Return computed results
  • ✅ Queries - Fetch and return data
  • ✅ Status - Report operational state

Without RETURN (Action only):

Check Power
    Log    Power is OK
    # No data returned

With RETURN (Action + Data):

Get Power Level
    Log    Reading power
    RETURN    95.5
    # Caller gets the value 95.5

📝 RETURN Statement Syntax

*** Keywords ***
Calculate Sum
    [Arguments]    ${a}    ${b}
    ${result}=    Evaluate    ${a} + ${b}
    RETURN    ${result}

Get Status
    RETURN    operational

Get Multiple Values
    RETURN    value1    value2    value3

Capturing Return Values:

*** Test Cases ***
Math Test
    ${sum}=    Calculate Sum    5    3
    Log    Sum is ${sum}

Status Test
    ${status}=    Get Status
    Should Be Equal    ${status}    operational

Multiple Values Test
    ${v1}    ${v2}    ${v3}=    Get Multiple Values

📋 RETURN Statement Rules

  • 🔹 Syntax: RETURN value (capital RETURN)
  • 🔹 Position: Usually last statement in keyword
  • 🔹 Multiple values: RETURN val1 val2 val3
  • 🔹 Capture: ${var}= Keyword Name
  • 🔹 Optional: Keywords without RETURN return None

🎯 Your Task

Create a keyword that returns 'operational'. Capture that value in a variable and verify it with Should Be Equal!
